newsitem.title: UK: CRICKET-GILLESPIE GIVES AUSTRALIA PRE-TEST BOOST.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-GILLESPIE GIVES AUSTRALIA PRE-TEST BOOST.

text.p: Paceman Jason Gillespie seized three Hampshire wickets for seven runs in eight overs to thrust Australia to a confidence-boosting win on Monday ahead of the third Ashes test.
The touring team won by an innings and 133 runs after Hampshire, 309 behind on first innings, were dismissed for 176 on the third and last day.
Gillespie, who missed the drawn second test against England at Lord's because of a hamstring injury, finished with five for 33.
Australia's all-round performance here encouraged captain Mark Taylor as his side prepared to head for Manchester where the third test starts at Old Trafford on Thursday.
Taylor, whose team trail 1-0 in the six-test series, said: "We're starting to turn the corner, playing the sort of cricket I know this team can play. Morale has been good since Lord's.
"We couldn't have got much more out of this game than we did, and did everything pretty well right.

"After a three-day washout in out last match at Oxford, I thought we might be a bit slow but Jason Gillespie, Mike Kasprowicz and Paul Reiffel bowled really well. They all congratulated each other afterwards, and that's the sort of spirit I want to see in a touring team."
Hampshire, 71 for two overnight, were sent into a decline from which they never recovered by Gillespie's three-wicket burst.
He ran in fast and accounted for England discard Robin Smith, after a fighting effort of 44 in 150 minutes, Will Kendall and captain John Stephenson, yorked for a first-ball duck.

Shaun Udal (21) held up the touring side as black clouds loomed, but Shane Warne spun a delivery round his legs, and paceman Michael Kasprowicz provided the knockout punch with a post-lunch spell of three for 32.
